prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1035; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A dated inspection photo shows the same dent before this crash.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officers responded to a side-impact collision at an intersection in Katy, Texas. Driver 1 was operating a sedan northbound and was struck on the driver's side by a pickup operated by Driver 2, who was southbound and turning left. Driver 1 reported pain in the left knee, which is consistent with the force and direction of the impact. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat and was present at the scene. Officers and on-scene statements confirmed Driver 1 was inside the vehicle at the time of the crash. No independent witnesses to the collision were located. Scene photographs confirm the general position of both vehicles and the location of the damage. The damage to the sedan is largely consistent with the reported impact. A prior inspection photograph of the sedan shows a dent in the same area, which was not addressed in either driver's account. Driver 1 reportedly lives in the same household as the policyholder. Both drivers were cited for further review, and the investigation remains open pending follow-up.
